sources.title: Sierra Leone Immigration Department: official eVisa service link
sources.officialityEvidence: The current Sierra Leone Immigration Department homepage on slid.gov.sl identifies its eVisa link as the Official Portal and directs applicants to evisa.sl.
sources.supportingExcerpt: Apply eVisa Official Portal Apply online via the official Sierra Leone eVisa portal.

sources.title: Sierra Leone eVisa: live terms and FAQ frontend text
sources.publisher: Ministry of Internal Affairs / Sierra Leone Immigration eVisa service
sources.officialityEvidence: SLID directly links www.evisa.sl as its official eVisa portal; the current portal frontend loads this live translation bundle, which contains both the terms and FAQ/home issuance instructions.
sources.supportingExcerpt: If your eVisa application is accepted, we will be sending you the eVisa as an email attachment.

sources.title: Sierra Leone eVisa: live nationality form selector
sources.officialityEvidence: The official evisa.sl frontend configured by SLID calls this endpoint after nationality selection. The endpoint’s empty JSON response means no current electronic form is exposed for Burkina Faso, despite the terms rule.

sources.title: Sierra Leone eVisa: live Mali nationality-form result
sources.officialityEvidence: The official evisa.sl frontend configured by SLID calls this endpoint after nationality selection. The endpoint’s empty JSON response means no current electronic form is exposed for Mali, despite the terms rule.

sources.title: National Tourist Board: Visa-on-arrival to Sierra Leone
sources.officialityEvidence: The National Tourist Board publishes the 19 November 2019 Government visa-on-arrival announcement on ntb.gov.sl. The page remains live on the current Board site, whose footer says VOA operates, but its issuance date creates a material currency risk. It is retained to explain the unresolved historic cohort, not to normalize a current nationality status.
sources.supportingExcerpt: a new Visa on Arrival policy has been rolled-out for persons from the following countries or blocs

sources.title: Protocol A/P.1/5/79 on free movement of persons, residence and establishment
sources.publisher: Economic Community of West African States Commission
sources.officialityEvidence: ECOWAS publishes the Protocol on its official domain. Article 3 directly establishes visa-free entry for Community citizens visiting a Member State for up to 90 days with the specified travel and health documents.
sources.supportingExcerpt: enter the territory of that Member State free of visa requirements for a maximum period of ninety (90) days.

sources.title: ECOWAS current Member States
sources.publisher: Economic Community of West African States
sources.officialityEvidence: The current ECOWAS member-state page on ecowas.int identifies twelve Member States, including Sierra Leone and eleven foreign catalog passport states.

sources.title: ECOWAS press statement on Burkina Faso, Mali and Niger withdrawal transition
sources.publisher: Economic Community of West African States Commission
sources.officialityEvidence: ECOWAS’s current official press statement says the three withdrawals took effect on 29 January 2025 and requires relevant authorities in and outside ECOWAS Member States to preserve visa-free movement until further notice.
sources.supportingExcerpt: allow citizens of the three affected countries to continue to enjoy the right of visa free movement

policies.title: Sierra Leone: current ECOWAS ordinary passports — visa-free entry
policies.summary: The ECOWAS Free Movement Protocol establishes visa-free entry for a Community citizen visiting another Member State for up to 90 days. The current ECOWAS roster maps its eleven foreign Member States; the eVisa terms also exclude all ECOWAS members from the electronic service.
conditions: Article 3 requires a valid travel document and international health certificate and gives a maximum 90-day stay. Immigration retains admissibility and public-order controls under the Protocol.
The current twelve-State roster excludes Burkina Faso, Mali and Niger following their withdrawal; the separately documented transitional treatment applies to all three below.
This policy does not decide residence, work, transit, crew, diplomatic, official, service, special documents, individual admissibility or any bilateral arrangement.

policies.title: Sierra Leone: Burkina Faso, Mali and Niger ordinary passports — ECOWAS transitional visa-free movement
policies.summary: Although Burkina Faso, Mali and Niger are no longer shown on ECOWAS’s current twelve-State roster, ECOWAS’s withdrawal transition instruction requires Member-State authorities to continue visa-free movement for citizens of all three until further notice. Sierra Leone is an ECOWAS Member State.
conditions: This is a temporary ECOWAS transition, not a current membership classification. It remains subject to a contrary later notice, ordinary admission controls, travel-document and health requirements.
Article 3 supplies a maximum 90-day visitor scope and requires a valid travel document and international health certificate; Article 4 preserves public-order and inadmissibility controls.
It does not establish residence, work, transit, crew, diplomatic, official, service or special-document treatment.

No current exhaustive ordinary-passport arrival schedule resolves whether this code is pre-travel electronic or border-issued, so the fallback status remains unverified.
